hero.badge: Signal in, order out · Sleep through the US open
hero.title: Quant made simple — anyone can plug in
hero.subtitle: No strategy code — and no all-night screen time. Connect Discord, Telegram, or TradingView signals to a pipeline: parse, risk-check, and route automatically. Notify only, confirm first, or auto-submit. **In UTC+8, you can sleep while US hours still execute.**
hero.trust1: No need to watch the US open — signals run automatically
hero.trust2: Start notify-only, then go fully automatic
hero.trust3: Broker keys encrypted at rest — never shown in plaintext
hero.trust4: Kill switch, risk controls, and records stay visible
hero.disclaimer: SigTrades does not provide or recommend trading signals and does not guarantee their timeliness, accuracy, or profitability. Execution is based entirely on third-party sources and rules configured by the user.
hero.architectureTitle: A clear path from signal ingest to broker fill
hero.architectureSubtitle: Multi-source ingest on the left, unified parse and risk in the middle, per-account broker routing on the right.
hero.securityTitle: Encrypted credentials — plaintext for no one
hero.securitySubtitle: Cloud broker App Keys, secrets, OAuth tokens, and private keys are encrypted before storage and only decrypted briefly in controlled execution services. IBKR / Futu run via local Agent — gateway credentials never leave your machine.
hero.securityEncrypt: **App keys, secrets, and private keys** are encrypted at write time. **They never appear in plaintext in the product UI, logs, or exports.** Even SigTrades staff cannot view your broker keys through the product or admin console.
hero.security1: No plaintext keys in the UI, logs, or export files
hero.security2: Staff cannot view plaintext broker keys via product or admin
hero.security3: We never share broker keys with third parties without your authorization
hero.trust: Local broker credentials stay on your machine; the cloud stores encrypted credentials and execution audit only.

pipeline.connectDesc: Webhooks, Discord, Telegram, and more enter one ingest layer.
pipeline.parseDesc: AI or rules parse each signal, then membership, risk, and route rules decide auto-trade or notify-only.
pipeline.executeDesc: Tiger, Longbridge, Schwab, and Alpaca execute in cloud; IBKR / Futu use the local Agent and report status back.

hero.flowTitle: From one text signal to broker execution, every step is traceable
hero.flowSubtitle: Status, idempotency, audit records, and failure notifications make sure silent failures do not hide in the workflow.
hero.featuresTitle: More than webhook forwarding: a trading operations system

features.rulesDesc: Each pipeline has its own parse rules, broker, and execution policy — run in parallel and pause independently.
features.riskDesc: Daily loss, trade count, position size, sessions, and kill switch are controlled centrally.
features.auditDesc: Track signal_id, order id, fill price, P&L, and protective-order failures.
features.notifyDesc: In-app, email, webhook, and FCM notifications cover critical state changes.

hero.brokerTitle: Cloud brokers and local gateways in one workflow
hero.brokerSubtitle: Tiger, Longbridge, Schwab, and Alpaca run through cloud APIs. IBKR / Futu connect through the local Relay Agent.
hero.finalTitle: Connect one pipeline — that is how quant starts
hero.finalSubtitle: Link a signal source and broker in minutes. Validate with notify-only, then turn on auto-trade. Pause anytime.

dashboard.ibkrAccessWebHint: Self-Service OAuth, cloud execution, no local TWS
dashboard.ibkrWebActivationNotice: Important: after you upload keys in IBKR Self-Service and save credentials here, the production API often takes overnight to 1–3 days to activate. Tests may return invalid consumer (401) until then — wait and retry; do not keep regenerating keys.
dashboard.usmartRegionHint: HK and SG have different apply portals but the same Open API. Pick the entity where you opened the account.
dashboard.tigerUploadHint: Upload tiger_openapi_config.properties from the Tiger developer portal (prefers private_key_pk1), or a PKCS#1 private key file (.pem/.key/.pk1). Account and Tiger ID are auto-filled. Paper accounts also use env=PROD — do not pick the sandbox/test environment. For TBHK license, also upload tiger_openapi_token.properties or paste the token.
dashboard.tigerEnvHint: This is only a label — paper vs live is determined by the account number.
dashboard.tigerApiHint: Enable OpenAPI in the Tiger Developer Center first, then obtain your Tiger ID, trading account, and private key. You can also export and upload the configuration file. TBHK requires a user token; TBNZ usually does not.
dashboard.lbUploadHint: Enter Longbridge OpenAPI App Key, App Secret, and Access Token. Choose sandbox (offline) or live (online). You can save multiple accounts.
dashboard.longbridgeApiHint: Create an application in the Longbridge Developer Center, then obtain its App Key, App Secret, and Legacy Access Token. The Access Token expires after 90 days by default.
dashboard.lbSecretsRequired: App Key, App Secret, and Access Token are required.
dashboard.schwabUploadHint: Save Client ID / Client Secret / Callback URL first; then click Connect & authorize on the account card.
dashboard.schwabOAuthHint: Per Schwab OAuth docs the authorize URL is only client_id + redirect_uri. Portal Callback must exactly match the field below (recommended https://127.0.0.1). App must be Ready for Use; use the same brokerage login as client.schwab.com. Success looks like https://127.0.0.1/?code=... — paste that full URL even if the page won't load.
dashboard.schwabCallbackUrlHint: Must match Developer Portal → Callback URL exactly (no trailing slash).
dashboard.schwabAutoCallbackHint: Preferred: set Portal Callback to the same auto-return URL; after approval you’ll land back here and we finish OAuth automatically. If Portal still uses https://127.0.0.1, paste the address-bar URL (codes expire in ~30s).
dashboard.schwabAuthorizeStep1: 1. The Schwab authorize page should be open — sign in and approve accounts.
dashboard.schwabAuthorizeStep2: 2. If Callback is https://127.0.0.1: the page may not load — paste the full address-bar URL (with code=). Paste auto-submits.
dashboard.schwabAuthorizeCodeTtl: Authorization codes expire in ~30 seconds and are single-use. Submit immediately after paste; on failure, open authorize again.
dashboard.schwabCallbackWorking: Callback received. Exchanging the code and linking your account.
dashboard.schwabSecretsRequired: Client ID and Client Secret are required.
dashboard.alpacaUploadHint: Alpaca executes in cloud through the Trading API. Choose Paper or Live and enter that account's API Key and API Secret.
dashboard.alpacaApiHint: Paper and Live use different API keys and endpoints. Validate the pipeline in Paper before switching to a live account.
dashboard.alpacaSecretsRequired: API Key and API Secret are required.
dashboard.ibkrWebUploadHint: Advanced: paste IBKR Self-Service OAuth credentials for cloud Web API execution (no local TWS). Do not run a TWS trading session at the same time. Multi-leg still uses TWS Agent.
dashboard.ibkrWebApiHint: Create a Consumer Key, Access Token, signing/encryption keys, and DH Prime in the IBKR OAuth Self-Service portal, then paste them below. Paper/Live is a label — use keys from the matching account.
dashboard.ibkrWebGenerateHint: Click Generate keys: private keys and DH fill in below; three files download (public_signature.pem, public_encryption.pem, dhparam.pem) for upload to IBKR. Then finish Consumer Key and Access Token on IBKR and paste them here.
dashboard.ibkrWebGenerateOk: Keys filled in; three IBKR upload files downloaded
dashboard.ibkrWebSecretsRequired: Consumer Key, Access Token, Token Secret, signature key, encryption key, and DH Prime are required
dashboard.usmartUploadHint: uSMART runs in the cloud via Open API. From Personal Center → My API, copy channel, public key, and private key.
dashboard.usmartApiHint: My API issues channel + RSA key pair. Each request is checked with private-key body signature (X-Sign) and X-Channel.
dashboard.usmartSecretsRequired: Channel, RSA public key, and private key are required.
dashboard.agentBindingHint: IBKR / Futu run via local Relay Agent. Pick a connection mode; the Agent must enable the matching port.
dashboard.agentBindingHostPortHint: Futu OpenD defaults to 127.0.0.1:11111. Orders use the account currently logged into OpenD.
dashboard.ibkrLocalSetupHint: Two steps: download and start the local Agent first, then install/log in to TWS and enable the API (socket port: paper 7497 / live 7496).
dashboard.futuLocalSetupHint: Two steps: download and start the local Agent first, then install/log in to Futu OpenD (default 127.0.0.1:11111). Mode must match OpenD paper/live.
dashboard.ibkrImportantTipIntro: After downloading and logging into TWS, complete the two steps below. Otherwise API orders may sit on “Transmit” and never fill.
dashboard.ibkrTwsConfigStep1Title: ① API → Settings: enable socket clients
dashboard.ibkrTwsConfigStep1Desc: Path: **Configuration → API → Settings**. Check **Enable ActiveX and Socket Clients**. Socket port must match your mode (paper 7497 / live 7496).
dashboard.ibkrTwsConfigStep2Title: ② API → Precautions: bypass order precautions
dashboard.ibkrTwsConfigStep2Desc: Path: **Configuration → API → Precautions**. Check **Bypass Order Precautions for API orders**.
dashboard.ibkrTwsConfigAfterClose: After closing, you can open this guide again anytime via **“TWS required setup”** on the right.
dashboard.ibkrImportantTipApiPath: Enable API: **TWS / Gateway** → **Edit** → **Global Configuration** → **API** → **Settings** → **Enable ActiveX and Socket Clients**. **Socket Port** must match your mode.
dashboard.ibkrImportantTipNote: This site’s IBKR modes currently target TWS (paper 7497 / live 7496). If you use Gateway, switch to its ports or run TWS instead.
dashboard.ibkrConnectionModeHint: Must match TWS → API → Socket Port (paper 7497 / live 7496). Orders use TWS's logged-in account.
dashboard.futuConnectionModeHint: Must match OpenD trading env (default 127.0.0.1:11111). Orders use OpenD's logged-in account.

dashboard.tigerKeepKeyHint: When editing, you can skip re-uploading the key to keep the saved private key.

timeline.detailUserRejected: You skipped this signal — no order was placed.
timeline.detailBrokerOffline: Local Agent or broker gateway is offline. Check Agent and TWS connection.
timeline.detailRoutingBrokerMismatch: Routing blocked: the pipeline’s broker account does not match any current binding (unbound, switched, or disabled). Check Brokers, or edit the pipeline and pick the correct account.
timeline.detailRoutingAmbiguousAccount: Routing blocked: multiple accounts exist for this broker and the pipeline did not pick one. Edit the pipeline and select an account.
timeline.detailRoutingNoBinding: Routing blocked: no usable broker binding. Connect an account under Brokers and select it in the pipeline.
timeline.detailAlpacaSingleLeg: Alpaca multi-leg order failed. Ensure Level 3 options are enabled; SPX/SPXW index options may be unavailable on retail accounts — try equity options (e.g. SPY) or IBKR/Futu.
timeline.detailLongbridgeNoCombo: Longbridge does not support multi-leg combo orders (e.g. PCS / vertical spreads). Parsing is fine — switch to IBKR / Alpaca / Futu, or send a single-leg signal.
timeline.detailBrokerNoCombo: This broker does not support multi-leg combo orders (e.g. PCS / vertical spreads). Parsing is fine — use a broker that supports combos (e.g. IBKR / Futu), or send a single-leg signal.
timeline.detailFutuOpendTooOld: Futu OpenD is too old for combo orders (place_combo_order). Upgrade OpenD to 10.x+, restart it, then retry. The Agent home screen also warns on connect.
timeline.detailFutuSimulateNoCombo: Futu paper trading does not support combo options (PCS / vertical spreads). Use a Futu live account, or validate the pipeline with IBKR in paper mode.
timeline.detailTigerBadContract: Tiger rejected the contract. Stocks need a plain ticker (e.g. TQQQ) on the equity channel; options need a real expiry/strike on the chain (US equity options usually expire Fridays; keep test strikes near the market).
timeline.detailTigerEnvMismatch: Tiger account API rejected the request. Paper accounts should use production (env=PROD) with matching tiger_id/key; sandbox needs a separate tiger_id.
timeline.detailTigerAccountForbidden: Tiger rejected the bound account (code=1200). The API key/tiger_id is often still valid, but this paper account is blocked for assets/trading — check paper status in the Tiger app, or rebind a working account (do not confuse live with paper).
timeline.detailTigerComboSession: Tiger rejected this combo. Credit verticals need a limit order with a negative limit price (net credit). If it still fails with a negative limit during the regular session, the account is often temporarily unavailable — check Tiger account status.
timeline.detailTigerRateLimit: Tiger API is truly rate-limited (code=5 / HTTP 429). Slow down and retry.
timeline.detailBrokerConnectFailed: Broker connection failed. Check the raw error in execution details; for Tiger, verify paper vs live environment and account id.
timeline.detailAlpacaIndexOptions: Alpaca does not currently support US index options such as SPX/SPXW (us_index). Multi-leg (mleg) works for equity/ETF options — use SPY or switch to IBKR/Futu for index options.
timeline.detailRoutingNoReport: No execution report from the broker (service restart or unsupported order type). Refresh or check your broker app.
timeline.detailExpiredGeneric: Order expired — confirmation may have timed out, or the order could not complete in time.

terms.title: Terms of Service
terms.intro: By using SigTrades you agree to these terms. Please read them before continuing.

sections.title: What SigTrades is
sections.body:
SigTrades is a signal follow-trading automation platform that helps you connect third-party signal sources, parse messages, and route orders to brokers.

Important: SigTrades does not generate, edit, or recommend any trading signals or investment advice. All trade intents on the platform come from signal sources you configure. We make no guarantees about signal accuracy, timeliness, or profitability.

sections.title: Your responsibilities
sections.body: You must have lawful authority over the signal sources and broker accounts you connect, and you bear all trading and compliance risk. SigTrades is not liable for losses caused by signal content, market moves, or broker API issues.

sections.title: Service changes
sections.body: We may change features or pause service for product, compliance, or infrastructure reasons, and will notify you when practical. Paid entitlements are as shown on the pricing page and membership center.

refund.title: Refund Policy
refund.intro: This policy explains how Pro subscription billing and refunds work.

sections.title: Billing
sections.body: Pro is billed monthly via Stripe. By checking “Selecting means agreeing to billing rules” and completing checkout, you authorize recurring charges at the price shown at purchase.

sections.title: Cancellation
sections.body: You may cancel renewal anytime in the Stripe customer portal from the membership page. The current period is not refunded, but Pro access continues until the period ends.

sections.title: Refund requests
sections.body: For duplicate charges or system errors, contact support@sigtrades.com within 7 days of the charge with your account email and invoice details. We will review and process eligible refunds.

sections.title: Non-refundable cases
sections.body: Voluntary cancellation, substantial use of the billing period, or account suspension for terms violations are generally not refundable.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: We take privacy seriously, especially broker API credentials. Security and least privilege are design baselines.

sections.title: Information we collect
sections.body: Account email, language preference, subscription status, and configuration you provide (broker credentials, signal sources, pipelines). We do not sell your personal data.

sections.title: Encrypted broker credentials
sections.body:
Cloud broker credentials (Tiger, Longbridge, Schwab, Alpaca, and others) — **App Keys, secrets, OAuth tokens, and private keys** — are **encrypted before storage**. They are only decrypted briefly in controlled execution services for order routing. **Plaintext never appears in the product UI, admin console, logs, or exports.**

**Even SigTrades staff cannot view your broker key plaintext through the product or admin tools.** We do not share keys with any third party without your authorization.

sections.title: Local agent credentials
sections.body: IBKR and Futu bindings via local agents keep **secrets on your device**. The cloud only stores binding identifiers and routing metadata — **not local private keys**.

sections.title: Security & your rights
sections.body: We use encryption in transit, access controls, and least-privilege practices. Contact support@sigtrades.com to request export or deletion of account data (except billing records we must retain by law).
